the design of an ALOHA-like protocol for a channel with multiple-packet reception capability, under the constraint that the packets have to be transmitted within strict delivery deadlines.

this work has developed a novel theoretical framework to study the performance of slotted ALOHAs under multiple-packet reception, with the delivery deadline constraint, for the first time in literature.
this paper has developed a novel and efficient approach for the design of the slotted ALoHA protocol in MPR channels with delivery deadline constraints.

the proposed algorithm can be applied to the slotted ALoHA protocol in a channel with MPR capability to improve the performance of the system in the sense that the SDP is improved, which is a measure for the reliability in the system, and the throughput is increased, which is a performance measure in the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the optimal transmission probability for any $M$ and $D$ can be obtained by a fixed-point iterative algorithm, which can be implemented in a distributed manner for dynamic scenarios with near-optimal performances.
the optimal slotted ALOha with delivery deadline D is characterized, and a distributed algorithm is developed for the scenario that N is unknown and changing.

the optimal slotted ALOHAs for throughput maximization (D = 1) and deadline-constrained delivery (D > 1) are derived, and the corresponding distributed algorithms are proposed to achieve near-optimal performance in dynamic scenarios.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the MPR channel with delivery deadline constraint, it is possible to achieve near-optimal performance with a simple and distributed algorithm.
, in MPR channels, the SDP is maximized when the transmission probability is inversely proportional to the square-root of N, regardless of the value of M and D.
, by leveraging the MPR capability, the SDP of a packet can be greatly improved.
